When annealing radiolabeled complementary oligonucleotides, only the forward strand is labeled, and not both the forward and reverse strands at the same time. T4 PNK kinase is more efficient at phosphorylating single-stranded DNA. Furthermore, background bands may be present in EMSAs due to the presence of radiolabeled single-stranded DNA binding to endogenous proteins. Addition of excess unlabeled reverse strand drives annealing efficiency to produce double-stranded DNA and ensure there will be very little single-stranded DNA to bind to endogenous proteins.

In this section the radiolabelled probes are purified prior to mixing them with the proteins of interest to assess binding.43.Gather Quick Spin Columns for radiolabeled DNA purification (Sephadex G-25 columns, Sigma-Aldrich company) (stored at 4°C) to purify the radiolabeled probes. For each probe you will need two collection tubes, one lid, one column and two 15 mL conical tubes (conical tubes not included in the Sephadex G-25 column kit) (Figure 1).44.Shake or vortex the columns to break up the material inside to ensure even distribution.45.Open the top of the column then remove the bottom. Place bottom of the column into a collection tube and place the column and collection tube into the 15 mL conical tube. Repeat for all columns.a.Label the remaining collection tubes with the probe names.46.Centrifuge the 15 mL conical tubes at 1,100 × g for 1.5 min to collect the liquid from the column in the collection tube.47.Open the lid of the 15 mL conical tube and use tweezers to remove the column then the collection tube. Discard the liquid in the collection tube. Reassemble the collection tube, column and 15 mL conical tube.48.Centrifuge the 15 mL conical tube again for 1,100 × g for 1.5 min.49.Insert the dried column into the new, labeled collection tube and place the dry column/collection tube into a new 15 mL conical tube.Note: The powder in the column should appear dry and chalky after the second spin. If it still appears moist, centrifuge again to remove all residual liquid.50.Spin cooled radiolabeled probes in tabletop mini centrifuge to collect liquid at the bottom of the tube.51.Open the lid of the 15 mL conical tube and transfer the entire radiolabeled probe (50 μL) onto the top of the column. Ensure you do not touch any other part of the column set up with the pipette tip.52.Place the conical tube lid back on and centrifuge at 1,100 × g for 4 min.a.During the spin, place the column lids on the Perspex tube container by aligning the ring of the collection tube lid with the opening of the Perspex box tube hole (Figure 1).53.Use long forceps to carefully remove and discard the dried column.54.Use long forceps to carefully transfer the collection tube containing the purified probe into the ring (Figure 1). Press the collection tube firmly down into the ring, close the lid and place purified probes in at 4°C. Check the forceps for any radioactive contamination between transferring each probe.Pause point: Proceed immediately to non-denaturing polyacrylamide gel set up or continue another day. 32P has a half-life of 14.3 days.

steps.title: Prepare EMSA stock solutions
steps.instruction: Make all buffers and reagents required for electrophoretic mobility shift assays (EMSAs) as listed below, filter 0.22 µm and store at the indicated temperatures.

substeps.instruction: Buffer A (500 mL total, store 4 °C ≤6 months): 5 mL 1 M HEPES pH 7.8 (final 10 mM), 750 µL 2 M MgCl₂ (final 1.5 mM), 2.5 mL 1 M KCl (final 10 mM), add Milli‑Q water to 491.8 mL.

Buffer C (100 mL total, store 4 °C ≤6 months): 2 mL 1 M HEPES pH 7.8 (final 20 mM), 25 mL 100 % glycerol (final 25 %), 8.4 mL 5 M NaCl (final 420 mM), 150 µL 1 M MgCl₂ (final 1.5 mM), 40 µL 0.5 M EDTA (final 0.2 mM), add Milli‑Q water to 64.4 mL.
10× TNE buffer (50 µL total, fresh): 5 µL 1 M Tris pH 8.0 (final 100 mM), 5 µL 5 M NaCl (final 500 mM), 1 µL 0.5 M EDTA (final 10 mM), 39 µL Milli‑Q water.

10× Gel‑shift buffer (50 mL total, store ≤3 years 20‑25 °C): 5 mL 1 M HEPES pH 7.8 (final 100 mM), 12.5 mL 2 M KCl (final 500 mM), 2.5 mL 1 M MgCl₂ (final 250 mM), 1 mL 0.5 M EDTA (final 10 mM), 25 mL 100 % glycerol (final 50 %), add Milli‑Q water to 4 mL.
10× TBE buffer (1 L total, store ≤6 months 20‑25 °C): 900 mM Tris (900 g), 900 mM boric acid (55 g), 50 mM EDTA (19.3 g), add Milli‑Q water to 1 L.
25 % (w/v) ammonium persulfate (APS): dissolve 250 mg APS in 1 mL Milli‑Q water; store 4 °C ≤1 month.

1 mg/mL poly dI·dC: add 1 mL Milli‑Q water per 13 U poly dI·dC powder (≈13 U/mg), invert, sonicate 3 min (30 s on/30 s off, high, no cooling), aliquot 1.5 mL tubes, heat 100 °C 1 min, cool slowly, store −20 °C ≤3 years.

steps.title: Prepare crystallography stock solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare all media, antibiotics, metal salts, buffers and other reagents needed for bacterial expression, purification and downstream assays, filter 0.22 µm and store as indicated.

substeps.instruction: LB medium (1 L): autoclave 10 g NaCl, 5 g yeast extract, 5 g tryptone, 10 g Milli‑Q water; store at room temperature.
1 M IPTG: dissolve 7.14 g IPTG in ~25 mL water, bring to 30 mL, filter (0.22 µm), aliquot 1 mL, store −20 °C.
100 mg/mL ampicillin: dissolve 4 g ampicillin in ~30 mL water, bring to 40 mL, filter (0.22 µm), aliquot 1 mL, store −20 °C.
0.1 M TCEP: dissolve 0.0287 g TCEP in ~0.5 mL water, adjust pH 7.5 with 2 M NaOH, bring to 1 mL, filter (0.22 µm), aliquot 0.2 mL, store −20 °C.
Protease inhibitor cocktail (1 tablet/1 mL): dissolve one tablet cOmplete Mini EDTA‑free EASYpack in 0.8 mL water, bring to 1 mL, aliquot 0.25 mL, store −20 °C.
1 M MgSO₄: dissolve 12.04 g MgSO₄ in ~90 mL water, bring to 100 mL, filter (0.22 µm), autoclave 121 °C 20 min, store 4 °C.
1 M ZnSO₄: dissolve 16.15 g ZnSO₄ in ~90 mL water, bring to 100 mL, filter, autoclave, store 4 °C.
1 M CaCl₂: dissolve 11.10 g CaCl₂ in ~90 mL water, bring to 100 mL, filter, autoclave, store 4 °C.
50 % (w/v) glucose: dissolve 50 g glucose in ~80 mL water, bring to 100 mL, filter, autoclave 115 °C 30 min, store 4 °C.

LeMaster‑Richards minimal medium (LR): dissolve 24 g KH₂PO₄, 5 g NaOH, 0.5 g NH₄Cl in 980 mL water, adjust pH 7.0 with H₂SO₄, autoclave 121 °C 20 min; add 100 µL CaCl₂, 100 µL ZnSO₄, 2.2 mL MgSO₄, 5 mL glucose just before use.
GST binding buffer (1 L, store 4 °C): 20 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.5, 1 M NaCl; add DNase I and protease inhibitor cocktail immediately before use.
GST elution buffer (100 mL, fresh): 20 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.5, 1 M NaCl, 30 mM reduced glutathione; make fresh before use.
TEV cleavage buffer (1 L, store 4 °C): 20 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.5, 400 mM NaCl; prepare fresh.
Gel‑filtration buffer (1 L, store 4 °C): 20 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.5, 1 M NaCl; ultrasonicate to remove bubbles.
DNA binding buffer (1 L, store 4 °C): 20 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.5, 150 mM NaCl; prepare fresh.
ITC titration buffer (500 mL, store 20 °C): 20 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.5, 150 mM or 300 mM NaCl; degas before use.

steps.title: Culture and transfect COS‑7 cells
steps.instruction: Grow COS‑7 cells, seed, and transfect with ZBTB7A zinc‑finger plasmids using FuGENE 6.

substeps.instruction: Grow COS‑7 cells in 10 cm dishes in DMEM + 10 % FCS + 1 % PSG at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.
Passage with 0.05 % trypsin‑EDTA for 5 min at 37 °C; reseed 24 h before transfection to reach 50‑60 % confluence.
Warm DMEM (with supplements) and Opti‑MEM (no supplements) to 37 °C for ~15 min.
In a 1.5 mL tube add 5 µL of 1 mg/mL pcDNA3 ‘empty’ plasmid (5 µg total) – repeat for each ZBTB7A ZF construct.
In a second 1.5 mL tube add 85 µL Opti‑MEM + 15 µL FuGENE 6; incubate RT 5 min.
Add FuGENE 6/Opti‑MEM drop‑wise onto the plasmid tube, mix gently, incubate RT 15 min.
During incubation, add 10 mL fresh warmed DMEM (10 % FCS, 1 % PSG) to each plate, label plates.
After 15 min, add the entire FuGENE 6/Opti‑MEM/plasmid mixture dropwise to the cells in a spiral pattern, gently rock plate to distribute.
Return plates to 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ incubator for ~48 h (do not exceed 72 h).

steps.title: Harvest COS‑7 cells and perform nuclear extraction
steps.instruction: Collect transfected cells, isolate nuclei, and extract nuclear proteins (NXT) for EMSA.

substeps.instruction: Discard media, add 1 mL ice‑cold PBS to each plate, scrape cells, transfer to 1.5 mL tube, keep on ice.
Centrifuge 300 × g 5 min, discard supernatant. (Optional: freeze pellet at −80 °C ≤3 months.)
Prepare fresh Buffer A and Buffer C (per mL add 5 µL 0.2 M PMSF, 5 µL 1 M DTT, 10 µL 1 mg/mL leupeptin, 10 µL 1 mg/mL aprotinin). Keep on ice.
Resuspend pellet in 300‑400 µL Buffer A (≈10× pellet volume), incubate on ice 10 min.
Vortex 10 s, spin 10 s in mini‑centrifuge, discard supernatant (cytoplasmic extract).
Resuspend nuclei in 50‑100 µL Buffer C (≈1‑2× pellet volume), incubate on ice 20 min.
Pre‑chill a 4 °C centrifuge and tubes; centrifuge 18 407 × g 3 min at 4 °C.
Transfer supernatant (nuclear extract) to a pre‑chilled tube; keep on ice (measure protein at 280 nm if desired).
Store NXT at −80 °C ≤1 month; thaw on ice before use.

steps.title: Dilute DNA oligos to 15 µM
steps.instruction: Prepare 15 µM working stocks of wild‑type and mutant −200γ forward and reverse oligonucleotides.

substeps.instruction: In a 1.5 mL tube add 15 µL 100 µM forward oligo + 85 µL Milli‑Q water (total 100 µL) → 15 µM forward stock; repeat for each forward oligo.
In a separate 1.5 mL tube add 15 µL 100 µM reverse oligo + 85 µL water → 15 µM reverse stock.

steps.title: Prepare labeling master mix for forward oligos
steps.instruction: Create an ‘n+1’ master mix for each forward oligo to be radiolabeled with γ‑32P ATP.

substeps.instruction: For each forward oligo: add 6 µL Milli‑Q water, 1 µL PNK buffer, 1 µL T4 PNK (10 000 U/mL) in a 1.5 mL tube; keep on ice.
Place tubes in a cold block or on ice.
Add 1 µL γ‑32P ATP (250 µCi) to each master mix tube, spin briefly, close tightly.

steps.title: Radiolabel forward oligos and anneal
steps.instruction: Label forward oligos with γ‑32P ATP, heat, and anneal with excess reverse strand to generate double‑stranded probes.

substeps.instruction: Aliquot 9 µL of each forward master mix into the corresponding forward‑oligo tube (contains 1 µL 15 µM forward oligo).
Incubate 30 min at 37 °C in a heat block (use Perspex shielding).
Set heat block to 100 °C, boil for 1 min (≈10‑15 min to reach temperature).
Spin tubes 10 s, keep lids closed, place back in Perspex container.
Add 40 µL reverse‑oligo mixture (32.3 µL water, 4 µL 10× TNE, 3.7 µL 15 µM reverse) to each forward tube, close, spin.
Place tubes at room temperature (20‑25 °C) for 4‑6 h (or overnight) to allow annealing.

steps.title: Purify radiolabeled probes
steps.instruction: Use Sephadex G‑25 spin columns to remove unincorporated nucleotides from each probe.

substeps.instruction: Equilibrate each G‑25 column (Sigma) by vortexing, then place column bottom into a collection tube inside a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge 1 100 × g 1.5 min; discard flow‑through, repeat spin to dry column.
Spin cooled probe tubes in mini‑centrifuge, transfer 50 µL probe onto top of column.
Centrifuge 1 100 × g 4 min; discard column, keep collection tube with purified probe at 4 °C.
Proceed immediately to gel setup or store (32P half‑life 14.3 days).

steps.title: Cast 6 % native polyacrylamide gel
steps.instruction: Prepare and polymerize a 6 % non‑denaturing gel for EMSA.

substeps.instruction: Clean two 18 × 16 cm glass plates with absolute ethanol.
Place 1.5 mm spacers (2 cm wide, 16 cm high) at each end of one plate, overlay second plate, clamp with 16 cm clamps.
Set assembly in casting stand opposite lower buffer chamber.
In a 50 mL tube combine: 39 mL Milli‑Q water, 2.5 mL 10× TBE, 7.5 mL 40 % acrylamide/bis (19:1), 200 µL 10 % APS, 50 µL TEMED. Mix by inverting.
Immediately pour solution into cassette, insert 12‑well comb, avoid bubbles.
Mark lane numbers, allow polymerization (≈20 min RT).
Transfer gel apparatus to 4 °C fridge 30‑40 min.
Prepare 0.5× TBE (25 mL 10× TBE + 475 mL water) and keep at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare EMSA binding reactions and load gel
steps.instruction: Combine nuclear extracts with binding buffer components and radiolabeled probe, incubate, then load onto the native gel.

substeps.instruction: On ice, label a 1.5 mL tube for each sample.

Add to each tube: 1.5 µL 1 mg/mL poly dI·dC (0.05 mg/mL final), 3 µL 1 mg/mL BSA (0.1 mg/mL), 3 µL 10 mM DTT (1 mM), 3 µL 10× gel‑shift buffer (1× final), 5 µL nuclear extract (volume adjusted to keep final volume 13.5 µL), and add Milli‑Q water to reach 13.5 µL total.
Keep all mixes on ice; optional supershift: add 1 µL anti‑FLAG antibody to designated tube before probe.
Spin probes briefly, add 1 µL radiolabeled probe to each sample, spin again.
Incubate samples on ice 4 °C 10 min to allow binding.
Remove gel from fridge, take off comb, fill lower chamber with 250 mL 0.5× TBE, flush wells with syringe.
Spin samples, load ~30 µL per well (add 6‑10 µL 6× loading dye if desired).
Assemble upper chamber, add 250 mL 0.5× TBE, place lid with electrodes.
Run gel at 250 V, 4 °C for 1 h 45 min (adjust time for probe length).
After electrophoresis, transfer gel to dryer, set 80 °C, ensure vacuum pump works, dry (≈10 min).
Image dried gel using phosphorimager.

steps.title: Clone ZBTB7A ZF region into pGEX‑4T1‑TEV
steps.instruction: Amplify, digest, ligate, transform, and verify the GST‑ZBTB7A‑ZF1‑4 construct.

substeps.instruction: PCR (22 µL total): 1 µL bone‑marrow cDNA, 1 µL 0.2 µM forward primer, 1 µL 0.2 µM reverse primer, 20 µL PrimeSTAR Max 2×, water to 22 µL. Spin, run thermocycler: 98 °C 5 min; 32 cycles of 98 °C 20 s, 55 °C 20 s, 72 °C 30 s; final 72 °C 5 min; hold 4 °C.
Run PCR product on 1 % agarose, gel‑extract (Omega EZ‑NA kit), measure concentration (260 nm).
Digest 1.5 µg PCR product with 1.5 µL NdeI + 1.5 µL XhoI + 5 µL 10× buffer, 37 °C 1‑2 h; purify.
Digest pGEX‑4T1 vector with same enzymes, purify.
Ligation (total 10 µL): 5 µL 2× ligation buffer, 4 µL digested insert, 1 µL T4 DNA ligase (TaKaRa). Incubate 16 °C 1‑2 h.
Transform 10 µL ligation into 100 µL BL21(DE3) competent cells (thaw on ice), incubate 20‑30 min on ice, heat‑shock 42 °C 60 s, ice 2 min, add 0.5 mL LB, recover 30‑40 min at 37 °C 220 rpm.
Centrifuge 5 170 × g 1 min, discard 450 µL supernatant, resuspend, spread 100‑150 µL on LB‑ampicillin (100 µg/mL) plates, incubate 37 °C overnight (12‑16 h).
Pick single colony, inoculate 5 mL LB + 100 µg/mL ampicillin, grow 37 °C 220 rpm 8 h.
Mini‑prep plasmid (AxyPrep kit), verify by sequencing with pGEX‑3′ primer, store −20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 13 % SDS‑PAGE gel
steps.instruction: Cast a 13 % resolving gel with a 5 % stacking gel for protein analysis.

substeps.instruction: Resolving gel (~3.6 mL): 0.6 mL water, 0.6 mL 80 % glycerol, 1.2 mL gel buffer (pH 8.45), 1.2 mL 40 % acrylamide/bis (29:1), 20 µL 10 % APS, 2 µL TEMED. Mix, pour, leave ~2 cm space for stacking gel.
Overlay with water, allow polymerization ~20 min RT, remove water.
Stacking gel (~1.6 mL): 1.0 mL water, 0.4 mL gel buffer, 0.2 mL 40 % acrylamide/bis, 20 µL 10 % APS, 2 µL TEMED. Pour on top of resolving gel, insert comb, polymerize 20 min RT, remove comb.

steps.title: Express and purify GST‑ZBTB7A‑ZF1‑4
steps.instruction: Produce recombinant GST‑ZBTB7A‑ZF1‑4 in BL21(DE3), purify via glutathione affinity, cleave with TEV, and perform size‑exclusion chromatography.

substeps.instruction: Inoculate 5 µL glycerol stock into 5 mL LB + 100 µg/mL ampicillin, 37 °C 220 rpm 8 h.
Transfer 1 mL culture to 100 mL LR medium + 100 µg/mL ampicillin, 37 °C 220 rpm overnight (12‑16 h).
Scale up: add 50 mL LR to 1 L LR (2 × 2.8‑L Fernbach flasks) + 100 µg/mL ampicillin, grow 37 °C 220 rpm until OD₆₀₀ = 1.0‑1.2 (≈3‑4 h).
Cool on ice, add 200 µL 1 M IPTG (final 0.2 mM), shift shaker to 16 °C, incubate 18‑24 h.
Harvest cells 3 590 × g 10 min 4 °C, discard supernatant, wash pellet with water.
Resuspend pellet in 40 mL GST binding buffer per L culture, transfer to 50 mL tubes.
Add protease inhibitor cocktail (1 % v/v) and 20 µL DNase I (20 U).
Lyse with high‑pressure cell disruptor 2‑3 min at 10 L/h (pre‑cooled to 6 °C).
Centrifuge lysate 24 300 × g 30 min 4 °C; keep supernatant on ice.
Wash 10 mL Glutathione Sepharose 4B column with ≥5 column volumes (CV) water then 5 CV GST binding buffer.
Incubate lysate with resin 6 h at 4 °C with rotation.
Load mixture onto column (1‑2 mL/min), wash ≥8 CV GST binding buffer.
Elute with 20 mL GST elution buffer, collect flow‑through, repeat elution.
Add 1 mg TEV protease (10 mg/mL stock, ~100 µL) to pooled eluate, dialyze against TEV cleavage buffer at 4 °C overnight (12‑16 h).
Assess cleavage by SDS‑PAGE.
Concentrate dialyzed sample to ~5 mL using Amicon Ultra‑15 3 kDa MWCO at 2 800 × g 4 °C.
Inject onto HiLoad 16/600 Superdex 75 pg column pre‑equilibrated with gel‑filtration buffer (1 mL/min); ZBTB7A‑ZF1‑4 elutes at ~80 mL.

steps.title: Run ITC binding assay and analyse KD
steps.instruction: Measure the thermodynamics of ZBTB7A‑ZF1‑4 binding to DNA using isothermal titration calorimetry and calculate dissociation constants.

substeps.instruction: Prepare protein and DNA samples in ITC titration buffer (20 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.5, 150 mM or 300 mM NaCl). Degas solutions.
Load protein (cell) and DNA (syringe) into MicroCal PEAQ‑ITC, perform a single‑site titration (typically 20‑30 injections).
Repeat experiment 1‑3 times (ideally three independent replicates) to ensure reproducibility; discard runs with large baseline fluctuations caused by bubbles.
Fit integrated heat data to a single‑site binding model using PEAQ‑ITC Analysis Software to obtain KD values.

description: Eukaryotic cells can be regulated by transcription factors that activate or repress gene expression. Many of these transcription factors contain small protein structural motifs known as zinc fingers that function as DNA binding domains. The functional versatility of zinc finger transcription factors is due to the amino acid residues within each zinc finger that allow for recognition of specific DNA sequences. Knowledge of transcription factor binding sites allows us to predict target genes. In vitro methods such as DNA-protein binding assays and X-ray crystallography can help to determine the precise DNA motif zinc fingers can bind to at a specific genomic region. The protocols below describe the detailed steps for structural and biochemical methods for studying the structure of ZBTB7A bound to the γ-globin -200 element (Yang et al., 2021). We first describe the expression of zinc finger (ZF) DNA-binding domains of ZBTB7A in mammalian cells and electrophoretic mobility shift assays (EMSAs) performed to explore protein-DNA binding in vitro. Next, we describe the procedures for the bacterial expression and purification of the C-terminal ZF DNA-binding domain of ZBTB7A. We then describe the procedures for crystallization of ZBTB7A in complex with -200 element. Lastly, we describe the isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) method to determine precisely how patient DNA mutations interfere with ZBTB7A binding. The protocol can be adapted to examine other eukaryotic and prokaryotic transcription factors and their interactions with target DNA sequences.
